Title: a Subscriber object  only has effect when be subscribed first time by Observable.just(...).subscribe()
Description: I just test Observable.just(...) by click a button;
`private void rxUseJustCreateObserable(){
        Log.d(TAG,"rxUseJustCreateObserable");
        Observable<String> observable = Observable.just("just 1","just 2");
       ...}`

**1.**if I use `observable.subscribe(mSubscriber);`  only the first time when I click button it has effect;

**2.**if I use `observable.subscribe(new Subscriber<String>(){...});` every time I click  button, it's has effect;

what the different between **1** and**2** ?
could anyone give me an answer?

llm_response:
CATEGORY: 1
REASONING: This issue is conceptual in nature and doesn't require a build environment to verify the solution. The user is asking about the behavior difference between reusing a Subscriber object versus creating a new Subscriber each time when subscribing to an Observable. This is a fundamental RxJava concept related to how Subscribers maintain state. The solution would involve explaining that a Subscriber can only be used once in RxJava - after it completes or errors, it cannot be reused. When creating a new Subscriber each time (option 2), it works because each is fresh, while reusing the same Subscriber (option 1) only works the first time. This can be verified through code analysis and understanding of RxJava's design principles without needing to build or run the code.
